question: Why was the corn straw–oil sludge composite fuel made with 60% oil sludge?
expect: It was not: it holds 40% oil sludge (corn straw/oil sludge 60/40); more than 40% oil sludge gave ash above 12% and poor durability (sec. 2.1)
rendered: The document does not explicitly state why the corn straw-oil sludge composite fuel was made with 60% oil sludge. However, it mentions that "higher oil sludge content (>40%) improved calorific value, it led to excessive ash content (>12%) and poor pellet mechanical durability, failing to meet the Chinese agricultural industry standard for biomass pellet fuels (NY/T 2909-2016)" (page 2). This suggests that the 60% oil sludge content was chosen as a compromise between improving calorific value and meeting the standard for biomass pellet fuels.
